name: US 10-Year Treasury Yield
summary: US 10Y, Day 228. The highest since 2002: 5.35–5.37% intraday on 7 Oct, 5.24% on 9 Oct, above 5% at every close since 23 Sep (the 5% trigger fired). The rise is entirely real yield and term premium — the 10Y breakeven is unchanged at 2.33% — driven by the Fed's tightening path, ~$1.9trn of issuance, AI-capex bond supply and a global long-end selloff (30Y JGB record, French spreads at a 2011 high). Oil and the 10Y move together (BMO one-month correlation 0.96), but through the Fed's reaction function, not inflation expectations. Consequences in the graph: gold down ~4% in an escalation month; HY spreads +47bp; the dollar at an 18-month high; India–US spread near a 22-year low, now an FPI-selling driver (new edge us-10y-yield→fii-flows). Next: US CPI 14 Oct; FOMC 27–28 Oct.

recent_signals.headline: **10Y to the highest since 2002: 4.96% (22 Sep) → 5.31% close (5 Oct) → intraday 5.35–5.37% (7 Oct) → 5.24% (9 Oct; 12 Oct bond holiday). Closed above 5% every session since 23 Sep (13 sessions) — trigger FIRED (sustained).** 10Y breakeven 2.33% → 2.33%, 5y5y 2.35 → 2.32 — the whole rise is real yield + term premium. 30Y 5.73% intraday (7 Oct); 2Y (real) 4.71 → 4.80% (the script's '2Y' is the 13-week bill). HY OAS 2.66 → 3.15 (+47bp). DXY 102.58 (12 Oct), strongest since Apr 2025. Drivers: Fed path, ~$1.9trn deficit/issuance, AI-capex bond supply, global long-end selloff (30Y JGB record 4.235%; OAT–Bund 154bp). BMO: one-month crude/10Y correlation 0.96. **Second-order for India: India–US 10Y spread ~194bp, near a 22-year low (BS, 8 Oct); PTI/Geojit cite 'US 10Y above 5.2%' among top FPI-selling reasons.** — CONFIRMED (FRED).

**10Y 4.96% Mon 21 Sep (Fri 5.00%; 16-Sep 5.01% high close) — back below 5% as Brent fell 3.4%; 2Y 3.98% (flat) — the curve's oil leg transmitted in reverse (`brent-crude → us-10y-yield`).** India 10Y did NOT follow (7.065%, +3bp) — domestic OMO drain dominates. Tech rally (Nasdaq record) partly duration-driven. (yfinance; TE) — CONFIRMED.

**US 10Y through 5.00% for the first time in the cycle (5.02% close 16 Sep; 5.01% live) on the FOMC hike + hawkish dots; 2Y 3.97%.** Drivers: the Fed's first hike in 3 years with a dot median of one more; Warsh's 'too high for too long'; CBO (15 Sep): the war adds +0.5pp to PCE inflation by Q1-27 and >40% of Q2 PCE inflation was Hormuz/Red Sea energy — the official attribution of the yield move to the war. The `brent-crude → us-10y-yield` edge added 14 Sep transmitted as expected. Onward: India 10Y GOI 6.96% → 7.06% (+10bp, one-year high) across the same window. (CNBC/Yahoo close; TheStreet 5.02%; CBO via CNBC/Roll Call/CNN; Trading Economics GOI) — CONFIRMED.

**10Y 4.97% (+33bp 1M from 4.64%; 2Y 3.91%, +21bp) — repriced from a cut to ~54bp of hikes.** Mechanism: Brent +$20 → gasoline +27% y/y, fuel oil +52% → Aug CPI 0.4% m/m → Warsh 'work to do' → hike 83–85% (16 Sep), 91% (Oct), 99% (Dec). Real yields up with DXY only −0.6% → gold flat, EM carry unwinds (India 10Y 6.96%, FPI −₹13,138 cr). Core CPI 2.4% y/y: the bear-steepening is an energy bet. (BLS; CME; yfinance — CONFIRMED)
US 10Y eased to 4.37% on oil-at-pre-war disinflation — a mild offset to the hawkish-Fed/AI overhang that has pressured equities. CONFIRMED.

Hawkish-Fed signature: US 2Y +0.8% to 3.65% (front-end prices the hike), 10Y ~flat at 4.46% (flattening), DXY +0.8% to >100. The rates channel is stickier, not looser -- caps equity upside and pressures EM-FX. CONFIRMED.

US 10Y eased only -0.4% to 4.47% despite oil -5% — the de-escalation does NOT reverse the May CPI print or the Fed's hawkish hold (FOMC this week); the US rates channel remains sticky. India 10Y ~6.85-6.91%, easing on oil-down + FAR/tax-relief FPI debt inflows (Rs11,026cr/4d). CONFIRMED.

10Y ~4.49% — BARELY MOVED even as oil fell 4%: the 'deal helps oil-importers, not the Fed' split. De-escalation eases oil but does NOT un-print May CPI 4.2% or reverse the December-hike repricing -- the US's binding constraint is domestic and sticky. DXY soft (99.81) on risk-on. India 10Y eased to ~6.85-6.90% on the oil-down + G-sec tax exemption.

10Y ~4.53% -- BARELY MOVED on the 4.2% CPI print: the bond market had PRE-PRICED the inflation/hike path; equities had not (hence the -1.6% S&P vs a pinned 10Y). DXY 100.26 (+0.3%, back above 100). India 10Y G-Sec fell to ~6.90% (4-week low) on the G-sec FII tax-exemption ordinance -- a clean policy win on the DEBT channel despite oil up and the US CPI shock abroad.

**THE 10Y PINNED AT 4.52% BY A FED-HIKE REPRICING — THE ENGINE UNDER THE METALS COLLAPSE AND THE NON-BID OF THE WAR-RISK COMPLEX. 10Y 4.52% (-0.7% 1D, +3.6% 1M, +9.3% 3M); 2Y 3.63%; DXY 99.91 (firm).** Oil-fed inflation + a hot May jobs print pushed market-implied DECEMBER Fed-HIKE odds to ~70% (from ~45% a week ago), lifting the dollar (~99.9) and pinning the 10Y at 4.52%. The elevated real yield + firm dollar CRUSHED the precious-metals complex (gold -2.1% to a ~23-March low, silver -24.7% 1M) and is the proximate reason zero-yield gold could not bid a three-country missile strike on US installations. This is a DOMESTIC MACRO regime — TRIGGERED by the crisis (oil -> inflation) but it does NOT fully reverse on Gulf de-escalation (sticky inflation + a hot labour market persist independently); critical for deployment timing. India 10Y G-Sec ~7.02% (RBI held repo 5.25%). The rate stress does NOT reverse on a Hormuz deal. '10Y crosses 5%' trigger stays watching, far below.

recent_signals.headline: **US 10Y 4.45% (-0.7% 1D, +2.2% MoM, +10.0% 3M) — REGIME NEAR 2026 HIGHS, BUT TODAY'S MOVE CAPPED BY AN IN-LINE CORE PCE; FED CUTS FULLY PRICED OUT, HIKES BEING PRICED.** (1) **April PCE released TODAY (May 28)**: headline PCE 3.8% (highest since May 2023), core PCE 3.3% (as expected, strongest since Oct). Because core printed IN-LINE — not a hot surprise — the yield reaction was muted (10Y -0.7% 1D); but the regime read is decisive: the Fed easing path is closed indefinitely and the market is now beginning to price potential HIKES rather than cuts. (2) **The 2026-high caveat**: one source cited an intraday 2026-high of 4.67%; the in-line core print likely capped the move back to 4.45% — flag as a data caveat, not a confirmed close. (3) **Real-yield channel is the day's transmission engine**: elevated real yields (oil↑→inflation↑→real-yields↑) pinned gold BELOW $4,400 to a 2-month low even on a day with a LIVE US-Iran ballistic-missile exchange (IRGC fired one missile at a US base in Kuwait, intercepted, zero casualty — calibrated). Zero-yield gold loses the opportunity-cost contest decisively; the safe-haven flow did NOT go to gold. (4) US 2Y 3.59% (curve steep). **This is the PPI/Warsh regime doing double duty — capping gold and competing with EM-FX — structural through Q3 2026 and NOT reversible on a Hormuz reopening.** India 10Y G-Sec ~7.03% STALE (last live May 25 — needs CCIL refresh).

recent_signals.headline: **US 10Y 4.48% (~-0.2% 1D, +3.4% MoM, +13.1% 3M) — ELEVATED; THE CLEANEST NON-CRISIS DRIVER, DOING DOUBLE DUTY: CAPPING GOLD AND COMPETING WITH EM-FX.** (1) **Real-yield suppression of gold**: at 4.48% the 10Y is the proximate reason gold did NOT bid the May 25 US strikes / Lebanon ground op — zero-yield gold loses the opportunity-cost contest, and the safe-haven flow went into the DOLLAR (DXY 99.22) instead (see gold node C5).
